short: The world's first operational nuclear-powered submarine, changing naval strategy forever.
full:
Commissioned on 30 September 1954, USS Nautilus (SSN-571) was the world's first operational nuclear-powered submarine. Under the direction of Admiral Hyman G. Rickover, its revolutionary propulsion system allowed it to remain submerged for unprecedented durations, freed from the need to surface frequently for air or fuel. In 1958, it famously completed the first submerged transit of the North Pole during Operation Sunshine.

Nautilus fundamentally transformed naval strategy, rendering conventional diesel-electric submarines largely obsolete for major blue-water roles. It demonstrated that submarines could operate as true underwater vessels rather than surface ships that only briefly submerged. Decommissioned in 1980 after a career spanning twenty-five years and over half a million miles, it is preserved as a museum ship in Groton, Connecticut.
